title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-03-24
lineage: SBD> MR> CASS> DAT> CDA> SHN> DAW(Bertha)> CDA/SHN

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of the March 24‑1973 Spectrum show with soaring vocals, killer jams and a standout second set
ai_review.review: The recording is an impeccably mastered Betty‑board SBD that delivers crystal‑clear instrument separation and balanced mix, only marred by occasional minor muffs. Musically the concert is a high‑energy showcase – Here Comes Sunshine, Dark Star (short but potent), Spanish Jam, Truckin', Playin’ in the Band, He's Gone, Row Jimmy and Bertha are repeatedly highlighted as fire moments, with Phil’s harmonies and Keith’s keys shining throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 70 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5‑star; comments praise both performance (energy, standout jams) and recording quality (pristine soundboard). The few minor criticisms do not affect the overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Betty‑board (Jay Ashley) mix is crisp, with superb instrument separation and clear vocals. A handful of reviewers note occasional muffs or brief drop‑outs, but the consensus is that the recording is pristine and fully listenable.

poor_songs: Donna's vocals (occasionally flat on a few tracks)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set rolls with tight transitions, especially the second‑set suite He's Gone → Truckin' → Jam → Spanish Jam → Dark Star → Sing Me Back Home. The first set is fluid and upbeat, leading into an explosive, jam‑heavy second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as solid, beautiful and soaring; guitar work praised for tone and energetic solos throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly lauded for powerful bass lines, harmonies on Box of Rain, and overall presence in the mix (often called ‘bombs’ or ‘heavy’).
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm‑guitar and vocal contributions noted as strong; occasional prominence of his vocals mentioned but generally positive.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards receive high praise – “crushing”, “perfect” and essential to the jams; mentions of Ron McKernan in historical context only.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart are praised for tight, driving rhythms; Billy’s kit work described as a highlight.
